title: Repair canonical Saw feasibility evaluator plumbing so truthful process facts reach the calculators
intent: Fix a manufacturing-authority defect in the canonical Saw feasibility path: the process facts a caller supplies (RPM, feed rate, tool/blade diameter, tooth count, stock thickness, machine power) were dropped before reaching the Saw calculators, so the evaluator scored on hardcoded conversion defaults regardless of the request. Extend the request/context path so those facts are delivered, guard the safety-critical facts to presence (missing -> UNKNOWN, out-of-range -> ERROR), and prove input-sensitivity with tests. Plumbing only: no thresholds, formulas, or favourable defaults are changed; neither Saw route is contained; SawLabService.check_feasibility and the compare route are untouched; the manufacturing-output inventory stays at 13.

diff_articulation.what_changed: RmosContext gained the machine/process fields _score_via_scorer already forwarded (machine_id, rpm, feed_rate_mm_min, spindle_power_watts, tool_diameter_mm, tooth_count) so pydantic v2 no longer silently drops them; _score_via_scorer now also forwards tooth_count. ScorerDesignSpec gained cut_length_mm. compute_saw_feasibility was extracted from rmos_feasibility_router.py into a new saw_feasibility.py (mirroring the existing profiling_feasibility.py extraction) so the added plumbing does not push the router past the 500-line file-size gate; the router imports it and registers it in _PRODUCTION_FEASIBILITY_ENGINES unchanged. compute_saw_feasibility gained a _SAW_REQUIRED_KEYS presence guard (missing -> UNKNOWN) and passes stock_thickness_mm/cut_length_mm from the request without friendly defaults. The router's _ENGINE_FAILURES now includes pydantic ValidationError so an out-of-range fact fails closed to ERROR instead of escaping as a 500. saw_engine._convert_to_saw_context reads the delivered facts (RPM/feed/diameter/tooth/power) instead of hardcoding max_rpm=5000 / feed=3000, falling back to prior defaults only on the ungoverned toolpath-generation path; _convert_to_saw_design prefers an explicit cut length. TC-09 and TC-20 witnesses now supply the required facts to reach the evaluator; a new test_saw_evaluator_plumbing.py proves facts reach the calculators, sensitivity, missing->UNKNOWN, out-of-range->ERROR, an unsafe rim-overspeed block, and documents the out-of-scope formula availability boundary.
diff_articulation.why: A feasibility lane that cannot see its own process facts is not evaluating the cut it was asked about; it produced a constant verdict regardless of RPM/feed/power. This is the authority defect Order 006 authorized repairing as a bounded, separate increment.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No prior change declares the RmosContext process fields or the compute_saw_feasibility missing-fact guard. Before this patch _score_via_scorer forwarded rpm/feed/power/diameter into a model that did not declare them, so pydantic v2's extra='ignore' dropped them and _convert_to_saw_context hardcoded 5000 RPM / 3000 mm-min. This patch is the first to close that gap and to fail closed on missing/out-of-range safety-critical facts.
diff_articulation.what_did_not_change: No calculator formula, threshold, weight, or favourable default was changed. Neither Saw route is contained. SawLabService.check_feasibility, the saw_compare route, and all G-code/geometry/generators are untouched. The manufacturing-output inventory is not regenerated and remains at 13 live-ungoverned rows with both Rosette rows FAIL_CLOSED. rosette/adaptive/profiling feasibility paths are unaffected (their RmosContext usage is unchanged and the new fields are optional).
diff_articulation.why_structural_extraction: compute_saw_feasibility moved into app/rmos/api/saw_feasibility.py. The router sat exactly at the 500-line file-size cap, so the added guard/fields would breach it; the profiling adapter was extracted from the same module for the same reason. The move is mechanical: the router imports the function and registers it unchanged, and the shared _score_via_scorer / ScorerDesignSpec (still router-owned, used by rosette too) are imported lazily to avoid an import cycle.

commands_run: test "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)"  # base is current
cd services/api && python -m pytest tests/rmos/test_rmos_feasibility_authority.py tests/rmos/test_rmos_governed_cam_path.py app/tests/rmos/test_saw_safety_gate.py -q --no-cov
proofs: Base SHA 52d9054d; merge-base equals origin/main tip (branch cut from current main).

New plumbing suite: 10 passed. Facts reach the calculators (rim_speed/bite_load/cutting_force metadata echoes the request); rim_speed/bite_load/power_ratio move when RPM/diameter/feed/power change; each omitted required fact yields UNKNOWN(ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE) naming the fact; rpm=50000 yields ERROR(ENGINE_ERROR); a 600mm blade at 9000 RPM blocks RED via rim overspeed.
TC-09 (evaluator-raises -> ERROR) and TC-20 (saw lane reaches saw calculators, differentiated from rosette) preserved by supplying the now-required facts; full affected suite 48 passed / 3 skipped.

Availability boundary: a 9,600-point in-range sweep produced zero GREEN/YELLOW verdicts. The block is driven by heat and deflection inheriting the calculator bundle's specific_cutting_energy default of 30 J/mm^3, a formula/units defect out of scope for this plumbing repair and reported for a follow-up increment; test_ordinary_job_still_blocks_pending_out_of_scope_formula_fix pins it.

The 30 J/mm^3 constant contradicts the repository's own governed material DB (app/data_registry/system/materials/wood_species.json: specific_cutting_energy_j_per_mm3 = 0.22-0.87 J/mm^3 per species, ~35-140x lower), and MaterialProperties bounds that field ge=5.0 so the truthful values are rejected outright - the fact cannot be wired without recalibrating the model. A second, independent deflection-model defect keeps deflection <30 even with a truthful kc forced in. Both are out of scope here.
Manufacturing-output inventory --check passes unchanged; live-ungoverned=13; both Rosette rows FAIL_CLOSED (neither Saw route contained).
Governance ratchets (file-size, bare-except, execution-class) pass from services/api.
verification.hardware: No physical-machine execution and no manufacturing output produced. Feasibility-evaluation plumbing and tests only.

files.intent: Declare the machine/process fields on RmosContext that _score_via_scorer already forwarded, so they are no longer dropped by pydantic v2.

Forward tooth_count; add cut_length_mm to ScorerDesignSpec; include ValidationError in _ENGINE_FAILURES so out-of-range facts fail closed to ERROR; import compute_saw_feasibility from the extracted saw_feasibility module and register it unchanged.

New home for compute_saw_feasibility and _SAW_REQUIRED_KEYS: missing-fact UNKNOWN guard, truthful design population, lazy import of the router-owned scorer adapter. Extracted to keep the router under the 500-line gate (mirrors profiling_feasibility.py).

Consume the delivered RPM/feed/diameter/tooth/power facts in _convert_to_saw_context instead of hardcoded defaults; prefer explicit cut length in _convert_to_saw_design; keep prior defaults only for the ungoverned toolpath-generation path.
Supply the now-required saw facts so TC-09 still reaches the (monkeypatched) evaluator and yields ERROR.
Supply the now-required saw facts so TC-20's saw lane reaches the saw calculators and stays differentiated from rosette.
New witnesses: facts reach calculators, sensitivity, missing->UNKNOWN, out-of-range->ERROR, unsafe rim-overspeed block, and the documented out-of-scope formula availability boundary.

findings: MEDIUM: edits the shared canonical feasibility path (RmosContext, _ENGINE_FAILURES, compute_saw_feasibility) and the saw conversion. Blast radius contained by making the new RmosContext fields optional (rosette/adaptive/profiling unchanged), guarding only the saw path, and preserving the ungoverned toolpath-generation fallback. Verified by the full affected suite and the manufacturing-output inventory --check (inventory unchanged at 13).
architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Plumbing-only authority repair. No formula/threshold/default recalibration; no route containment; no inventory change. The residual ordinary-job RED is a separate, out-of-scope formula/units defect, reported for a follow-up increment.
